steps.what: Check the order's recipient, address and delivery requirements
Prepare the working delivery sheet from verified order details
Pack and load the arrangements for safe delivery
Travel to the customer's delivery location
Deliver arrangements to the identified customer or authorised recipient
Enter the actual delivery outcome in the order record

tasks.design: Use the {OTHER} florist order system's native delivery view and an order-linked delivery-sheet template in {DOCS}. Physical packing, travel and customer handover remain unchanged, and the actual delivery outcome is recorded separately after handover.
tasks.previous_blocker: Verified recipient and handling details are copied from orders onto a working delivery sheet.
tasks.enabler_now: Native order views and editable document templates can reuse those details.
tasks.still_hard: Fragile arrangements, inaccessible locations and absent recipients.
tasks.human_edge: Protecting the arrangement and deciding whether the intended handover is actually possible.
tasks.altitude: Slightly less delivery preparation; the delivery responsibility stays unchanged.

evidence.claim: Native florist order views and editable delivery-sheet templates are model knowledge designs; the digest has no measured floral-delivery saving.

assumptions: Boundary models the task's direct-delivery branch, including its working sheet and actual order-status entry. It does not also add employee-supervision labour. In a supervision-only implementation, assignment, its communication and actual delivery records must be separately timed rather than inheriting these shares.

The {OTHER} category is the florist order system. The customer and order taker supply order ID, recipient, address, delivery window, contact and handling instructions in the existing order. s1 counts verification and manual clarification; missing or ambiguous addresses are not automatically resolved.

The designer confirms delivery fields while producing the working sheet in s2, retaining 6 hours of preparation. The designer observes recipient and delivery outcome in s5 and captures actual time, outcome and exception in s6; all 5 record hours stay. No free delivered flag or automatic customer notification is assumed.
Test native order views and templates first. No route solver or saving in physical travel is claimed. Ordinary author saves and the brief status save have no approval stage or click-saving benefit.
unknowns: Whether the role delivers directly or supervises delivery employees
research_questions: Does the native delivery sheet remove repeated copying while retaining all special handling instructions?

already_counted.description: Verify delivery details, check the sheet and record the actual outcome

incremental.description: Maintain delivery-sheet fields and sample missing instructions

approvals.approved_version: The actual arrangement, identified recipient and order-specific handover conditions checked at delivery; changed recipient or conditions require a fresh human decision

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1: B=100, R=94, gross=6, upkeep=0.5, net=5.5. Cautious case: an already useful order view removes no lookup and unusual recipient instructions retain 9.5 of 10 sheet hours; all other 90 hours stay, giving 0.5 gross minus 0.5 upkeep =0. High 3 retains more manual sheet correction than central.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Select flora and develop new combinations

steps.what: Read the existing arrangement brief and intended use
Inspect available flora and foliage for condition and suitability
Try numerous physical combinations to develop new floral creations
Select the flora and foliage combination for the arrangement

tasks.design: Keep physical material inspection, experimentation and final selection with the designer. The existing brief in {DOCS} remains an input; a generated image or stock template cannot establish the condition, balance and compatibility of the actual stems.
tasks.previous_blocker: The work depends on variable living materials and visual and tactile judgement.
tasks.enabler_now: No demonstrated software change removes that physical selection work in this boundary.
tasks.still_hard: Stem condition, weight, texture, colour relationships and the intended arrangement's physical balance.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing and feeling how actual materials work together.
tasks.altitude: The designer's work and decision rights stay unchanged.

reach.task: Explain a flower-quality requirement to a supplier

evidence.claim: Physical condition and combination judgement remain human in this task; the zero-saving boundary is model knowledge, not a measured local result.

assumptions: Boundary includes reading the real brief, inspecting materials, trying combinations and choosing them. It does not hide a written recipe or design record inside physical work: no such record is routinely produced in this modeled one-off selection. If a reusable recipe is actually written, that writing is an additional measured step rather than excluded labour.

The existing brief supplies occasion, intended scale, colour preferences and budget from order-taking work; s1 counts reading it and clarification. s2 produces observations of actual material condition, with all observation time retained. No structured freshness, suitability or sold-out flag is assumed.

Native brief views and existing stock records were considered; neither replaces inspecting and choosing the actual stems. No new tool is deployed, no extra maintenance is created and zero incremental upkeep is justified.
unknowns: Whether this business writes reusable recipes during material selection
Actual time spent looking up the design brief
research_questions: Does observation show a real record-writing or repeated lookup step beyond these physical selection activities?

incremental.description: No new software or maintained configuration is introduced

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1: B=100, R=100, gross=0, upkeep=0, net=0. Both ends retain all brief reading, inspection, experimentation and selection because no proposed change touches their actual work. An unobserved recipe-writing activity is not assigned an invented baseline.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Inspect flower condition and check quantities of usable supplies
Choose the flowers, supplies, quantities and supplier to purchase
Prepare the supplier order from the selected items and quantities
Check item varieties, quantities, price and delivery timing in the order
Submit the checked purchase to the wholesaler or grower
Record the actual supplier confirmation against the purchase

tasks.design: Use editable favourites or past-order lists in {PARTNER_PORTAL} to prepare the next order, keeping all item and quantity choices with the designer. Record the supplier's actual confirmation in the {OTHER} florist order system using an existing purchase reference; no automatic stock threshold or order submission is introduced.
tasks.previous_blocker: Frequently ordered supplies require repeated catalogue selection and purchase-reference entry.
tasks.enabler_now: Native favourites and reusable order references may remove those specific operations.
tasks.still_hard: Perishability, variable quality, future demand and supplier substitutions.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing what is usable and worth buying for the planned arrangements.
tasks.altitude: Less repetitive order entry, with unchanged buying and stock-quality judgement.

reach.task: Check a supplier's substitution against the actual requirement
reach.learn: Supplier pack sizes, quality grades and confirmation terms

evidence.claim: Supplier favourites, editable repeat orders and purchase-reference reuse are model knowledge designs; the digest contains no floral-purchasing case or measured saving.

assumptions: Boundary includes physical stock checking, item selection, order preparation, real submission and recording the actual confirmation. It adds no inventory record or par-level system; observed replenishment needs remain human observations in s1.

The designer produces supplier, item variety, grade, pack size, quantity and desired delivery date in s2 and captures and confirms those fields in s3, whose retained 15 hours include manual entry of unfamiliar items. Supplier offers provide price and availability; missing or changed data require manual checking in s4.

The supplier produces confirmation reference, accepted lines, substitutions and promised date after s5. The designer captures and verifies them in s6's retained 4 hours; a missing confirmation remains unresolved rather than becoming an accepted flag. The {OTHER} category is the florist order system.

Test native portal favourites and order references before custom integration. The author does not approve a same-system save; s6 saves only repeated reference entry, while s5 is the distinct external purchase action and stays fully retained.
unknowns: Availability of supplier favourites and usable purchase references
Share of repeat items versus seasonal or substituted purchases
research_questions: Do repeat-order features reduce entry time after correcting pack-size and variety defaults?

already_counted.description: Enter selected items, check the final order and verify the supplier confirmation

incremental.description: Retire obsolete favourites and check changed supplier pack sizes

approvals.approved_version: Exact supplier, item lines, varieties, quantities, prices and delivery date checked in s4; any changed line invalidates purchase approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1: B=100, R=89, gross=11, upkeep=1, net=10. Cautious case: seasonal varieties require nearly all current entry, retaining 24 of 25 order hours, and unmatched confirmation references retain all 5 record hours; all other 70 hours stay, giving 1 gross minus 1 upkeep =0. High 6 retains extra default correction beyond central.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Clarify the customer's intended location and questions about care
Identify the flower, foliage or plant and relevant handling concerns
Read the applicable care and handling guidance
Prepare the actual take-home care label for the purchased item
Hand the checked care label to the customer
Inform customers about care, maintenance and handling and demonstrate where needed

tasks.design: Organise checked supplier guidance and existing care-label templates in {DOCS}. The designer identifies the actual item, adapts the label and checks it, then separately hands it over and explains the care in person; no customer conversation log is added.
tasks.previous_blocker: Standard care wording is repeatedly found and copied onto the take-home label.
tasks.enabler_now: Native document search and editable care labels can reuse checked instructions without generating new plant-care advice.
tasks.still_hard: Identification, unusual mixed arrangements and matching advice to the customer's actual conditions.
tasks.human_edge: Demonstrating handling and noticing that the customer has misunderstood an instruction.
tasks.altitude: Less care-label preparation, with unchanged customer advice and demonstrations.

reach.learn: Item identification and when to seek specialist guidance

evidence.claim: Native care-guidance search and editable take-home labels are model knowledge designs; no digest product establishes floral-care advice savings.

assumptions: Boundary is the workflow that already gives a written care label along with spoken advice. The label is the customer's actual artefact, not an invented internal record. If the shop only gives verbal guidance or already uses fully printed labels, no label-writing benefit is claimed.

The designer produces the actual item identification and relevant customer context in s1-s2, retaining all 25 hours. Supplier guidance supplies item-specific watering, light, temperature and handling instructions; s3 counts reading and applicability checking. Unknown identification or conflicting guidance requires manual clarification rather than selecting a guessed template.

The designer captures selected item, guidance version and tailored care text while preparing and checking the label in s4, retaining 10 hours for selection, edits and checking. Handover and explanation remain in s5-s6. No automatic plant identification, maintenance flag or customer send is implied.
Test existing native care documents and label templates first. Ordinary template saves have no gate or saving; the gate covers handing the actual final label to the customer.
unknowns: Whether take-home care labels are currently written, preprinted or absent
Coverage and quality of existing supplier guidance
research_questions: How much care-label preparation is actually removed after item selection and checking?

already_counted.description: Check applicable guidance and adapt and verify the take-home label

incremental.description: Keep care labels aligned with current supplier guidance

approvals.approved_version: The actual customer-specific clarification during the live discussion
Exact item-specific label text and guidance version checked in s4; any edit or item substitution requires a fresh check
The live care explanation and handling demonstration for the identified item and customer context

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1: B=100, R=87.5, gross=12.5, upkeep=0.5, net=12. Cautious case: already printed labels or unfamiliar species remove no writing work, so the change is not deployed and all existing work remains with no new upkeep: zero. High 7 applies where editable labels are genuinely written today, retaining more item-specific adaptation than central.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
